clues: This town sits on the east bank of a wide river. It lies a long way northwest of a great port town.
Summer here is usually hot and humid, and heat waves can roll in for days.
In October 1812, this small river town was named the state capital. It has kept the job ever since.
On the Underground Railroad, folks who fled slavery stopped here. They found food and help in this river town, then went north.
The governor of Pennsylvania works in this town by the river. The men and women who make the state laws meet in the capitol here.
